persona.name: Birgitta
persona.background: Daughter of a sawmill foreman; family listened to Radioservice and Karusellen on the Radiotjänst set in the kitchen, 'Önskekonserten' on Sundays, folkpark dances in summer, older cousin bought 78s and later singles from the record shop on Drottninggatan.

seeds.song: Lill-Babs - Är du kär i mej ännu Klas-Göran?
The Soul Stirrers - Touch the Hem of His Garment

SE1955A.wouldSay: Snoddas! Pappa sang Flottarkärlek every time he'd had a dram. And Klas-Göran, we all sang that in the schoolyard. But who put this jazz in? That's what the men at Nalen listened to, not us. And Augustin was Brita Borg's song, everybody knows that.
missing: Evert Taube - Calle Schewens vals (1930s evergreen)
Bill Haley & His Comets - Rock Around the Clock (1955)
SE1955A.fake: Four of ten seeds are bebop, hard bop and US gospel that no ordinary Swedish family heard, the obvious foreign hits (Bill Haley, Elvis, Paul Anka) are absent, and Augustin is credited to the wrong singer's version; unsure whether 'Lilla stjärna' is the exact Alice Babs title I remember.

seeds.song: Lill-Babs - Är du kär i mej ännu Klas-Göran?
Harry Brandelius - Hur tokigt som helst
Lasse Dahlquist - De' ä' dans på Brännö brygga
Bill Haley & His Comets - Rock Around the Clock

SE1955B.wouldSay: Min mammas boogie, Lill-Babs was barely older than me when that came out! And Snoddas, and Brännö brygga, we danced to that at the folkpark every Midsummer. Then Diana and Elvis on Radio Luxembourg under the covers. Yes, this is it.
missing: Evert Taube - Calle Schewens vals (1930s evergreen)
SE1955B.fake: Little feels fake; the only doubt is 'Hur tokigt som helst', which I cannot place as a Brandelius hit, and the foreign rock-and-roll share skews to the late 1950s teen crowd rather than what my parents' radio played.

persona.name: Johan
persona.background: Son of a Husqvarna factory worker and a nurse; taped Tracks on P3 on Saturday evenings onto cassettes, watched Melodifestivalen and Eurovision with the family, parents played dansband at the summer dance pavilion, older brother into hard rock.

seeds.song: Modern Talking - You're My Heart, You're My Soul
Bucks Fizz - Making Your Mind Up
ABBA - The Winner Takes It All

SE1984A.wouldSay: Modern Talking? That was the winter after, '85. And Bucks Fizz, Dschinghis Khan... this is a Eurovision rerun from when I was ten. Where are Gyllene Tider and Herreys? Vikingarna, fine, that's my parents in the car.
SE1984A.fake: It opens with foreign Euro-pop from 1979 to 1981 and a Modern Talking single that only became a hit in 1985, has no Swedish pop or rock at all beyond ABBA and Secret Service, and pads out with US hip-hop and punk nobody in my class heard; local share is 5 of 13, well under two-thirds.

persona.name: Johan
persona.background: Son of a Husqvarna factory worker and a nurse; taped Tracks on P3 on Saturday evenings onto cassettes, watched Melodifestivalen and Eurovision with the family, parents played dansband at the summer dance pavilion, older brother into hard rock.

seeds.song: Gyllene Tider - När vi två blir en
Modern Talking - You're My Heart, You're My Soul

SE1984B.wouldSay: Diggi-Loo Diggi-Ley! The golden shoes, we won Eurovision! And Främling, my sister had the Carola poster. Sommartider, every school disco ended with that. Yes, this is 1984.
missing: Wham! - Wake Me Up Before You Go-Go (1984)
SE1984B.fake: Only small things: Jan Lindblad whistling Shenandoah is a TV curiosity rather than a hit, Modern Talking belongs to 1985, and several picks (Rivers of Babylon, Summer Night City, Just nu!) lean to 1978 to 1980 rather than the year itself.

persona.name: Guadalupe
persona.background: Daughter of a railway worker; radio on all day in the kitchen (XEW 'La Voz de la América Latina desde México' and local norteña stations), Siempre en Domingo on Televisa on Sundays, Pedro Infante and Javier Solís films on TV, bailes and quinceañeras with conjunto norteño and banda, older brother's cassettes of Los Tigres in the truck.

seeds.song: Cornelio Reyna - Me Caí de la Nube
Los Relámpagos del Norte - Ya No Llores
Los Tigres del Norte - Contrabando y Traición
Los Alegres de Terán - Carga Blanca

MX1975A.wouldSay: ¡Volver, volver! My father sang that at every party until my mother told him to sit down. And El Rey, and Javier Solís... ay, this is the kitchen radio on a Sunday. Contrabando y traición, Camelia la Texana, everybody knew that story.
missing: José José - La nave del olvido (1970)
MX1975A.fake: It is a ranchera-and-norteño version of Mexico with no balada, cumbia or Siempre en Domingo pop (no Juan Gabriel, no Camilo Sesto), no English-language hits at all, and a 1930s Texas conjunto recording (La Chicharronera) that no teenager in 1975 would recognise; I am unsure of the exact years of the Relámpagos and Alegres de Terán tracks.

seeds.song: Los Tigres del Norte - Contrabando y traición

MX1975B.wouldSay: Volver, volver, then Contrabando y traición, then Juanga with No tengo dinero, that's exactly how the radio went! And Eres tú, my sister learned it for the school festival. Yes, this is my house in 1975.
missing: Cornelio Reyna - Me caí de la nube (1970s)
MX1975B.fake: Nothing feels fake; it is short and leans on the canon greatest-hits list, with no cumbia, banda or English-language radio hits, so it may run thin after the first few songs.

persona.name: Cláudia
persona.background: Daughter of a bank clerk and a schoolteacher; family watched Globo novelas every night (Dancin' Days in 1978) and the soundtrack LPs sat by the radiola, Rádio Mundial and Rádio Tupi on the transistor, Chacrinha on Saturday TV, samba school rehearsals at Carnaval, discotheque matinées with friends.

seeds.song: Martinho da Vila - Canta, Canta, Minha Gente
Tim Maia - Gostava Tanto de Você
Benito Di Paula - Retalhos de Cetim
Odair José - Eu Vou Tirar Você Desse Lugar
Barry White - You're the First, the Last, My Everything

BR1978A.wouldSay: 'Abra suas asas, solte suas feras'... Dancin' Days! The whole country was dancing to the novela. Then Maluco Beleza and Elis, my mother cried at Como Nossos Pais. This is exactly 1978.
missing: Chico Buarque - O Que Será (À Flor da Pele) (1976)
Lady Zu - A Noite Vai Chegar (1977)
John Travolta & Olivia Newton-John - You're the One That I Want (1978)
BR1978A.fake: Very little; Roberto Carlos, the biggest-selling artist in the country, is missing, and I Will Survive was a 1979 hit here rather than 1978.

seeds.song: Sérgio Mendes & Brasil '66 - Mas Que Nada
Baden Powell & Vinicius de Moraes - Canto de Ossanha

Cartola - O Mundo É um Moinho
Milionário & José Rico - Estrada da Vida
Lindomar Castilho - Você É Doida Demais

BR1978B.wouldSay: Wave, Mas Que Nada, Summer Samba... this is what they play for tourists in the hotel bar. That was my parents' music from before I was born. Wait, Sandra Rosa Madalena! Now that's 1978, Magal on Chacrinha.
missing: Tim Maia - Gostava Tanto de Você (1973)
Rita Lee & Tutti Frutti - Ovelha Negra (1975)
BR1978B.fake: It opens with a 1960s bossa nova export compilation (Summer Samba and the Brasil '66 version were hits abroad, not at home), adds choro and piano recital pieces, and has no disco, no novela themes and none of the foreign hits that filled every party in 1978.
